_what_this_is: The written contract for what a cycle step READS. core/notary.py grades a step by the age of its inputs; until this file existed that list came only from the static scanner in core/cycle_graph.scan_requires(), which resolves literal paths and nothing else. A step whose paths are built at runtime scanned to [], [] means UNKNOWN provenance, and UNKNOWN means the gate refuses an irreversible action. This file lets a human WRITE the contract that the scanner cannot infer.
_the_rule: A declaration WINS over the scanner for the steps it names. A step not named here is untouched: scanner only, and the scanner's silence still means UNKNOWN, which still means refuse. This file has no syntax for weakening a step it does not mention, and if it is deleted, unreadable or malformed the system behaves exactly as it did before it existed.
_who_owns_it: A human. Named in safety/protected_paths.py, so no generated patch can write it at either enforcement layer. This is the one place where a step can be handed provenance it did not earn from a scan; a system able to edit it could declare itself trustworthy.
_how_to_add_a_step: Read the module the step actually calls and list what it opens on THAT path. Do not copy the scanner's output, do not guess from the step name, and record where the list came from in 'derived_from'. Paths are repo-relative POSIX; a directory means the whole tree (the notary takes its newest file's mtime).

web_intelligence.entry_point: web_intelligence_agent.run(axes_filter=...) — fast_cycle_runner.py:1289, launched as a subprocess with `import web_intelligence_agent as w; w.run(axes_filter=...)`. NOT the module's __main__ block.

_inputs_why.memory/web_intelligence: THIS STEP'S REAL INPUT IS THE LIVE NETWORK, AND THAT IS THE WHOLE PROBLEM. web_intelligence_agent.py reads NO config file and no upstream product: its axis table is a module literal (:159) and its substance arrives over requests/feedparser/ddgs/youtube_intel. Every file it opens on the run path is its OWN output — the per-axis domain files it re-reads to resume (:601, :610, :618), cycle_checkpoint.json (:632-638), and latest.json, which it writes and then reads back to verify (:834-841). All of them live under this tree. So the honest declaration is not a list of upstream dependencies; it is the artifact that evidences the fetch and says WHEN the world was last read. That is what the age dimension should mean for a VERIFIER. Declared as a tree because the step picks the dated folder at runtime; the notary grades a directory by its newest file.

web_intelligence._this_declaration_is_circular_and_here_i: STATED PLAINLY BECAUSE IT IS A REAL WEAKENING, NOT A DETAIL. The declared input is the step's own product, so running the step refreshes its own freshness. For web_intelligence the age dimension therefore becomes a LIVENESS check ('it ran recently') and NOT a staleness check ('what it read was recent'). WHAT THIS CANNOT CATCH: run() writes master_web_intel.json and copies it to latest.json unconditionally at the end (:830-838), so a night on which every fetch failed still refreshes the tree and still reports age=FULL. The verify-read at :841 asserts ready_for_self_observer but only WARNS. A sharper input would be one written only on a SUCCESSFUL fetch; none exists today. This is the narrowest honest declaration available, not the right one forever. THE CIRCULAR INHERITANCE IS SAFE, THOUGH, AND NOT BY LUCK: web_intelligence is in core/notary.VERIFIERS, so `level = own` and the inheritance loop is skipped — the step cannot lift itself by its own prior stamp. The verifier break exists for exactly this shape.

also_reads.memory/claude_query_proposals.json: READ at :112-117 and deliberately NOT an age input, for the same reason github_publish excludes cortex_memory/hypotheses/pending.json. It is OPTIONAL BY CONSTRUCTION: _load_claude_proposals() is guarded by .exists() and returns {} when absent, so listing it under 'inputs' would mean DELETING a dead file lowers the gate. MEASURED 31 Aug 2026: its mtime is 2026-05-16, 106.6 days old, which scores MINIMAL(1). Declaring it would hold web_intelligence at level_1 and keep the publish gate shut — it does not fix this, it re-breaks it one level higher.

A file that may or may not be read on any given night cannot carry the step's age honestly: declaring it as an input would make the gate depend on what a model decided to look at.
